comparisons.peer_topic: Revolving Credit Facility Terms and Status
comparisons.peer_summary: The Company has $3 billion available under a revolving credit agreement expiring on April 29, 2027, with no outstanding borrowings as of December 28, 2024, and interest rates tied to SOFR or Base Rate plus margins.
comparisons.comparison: Both Micron and AMD disclose having no outstanding borrowings under their respective revolving credit facilities at the end of fiscal year 2024. However, they differ in facility size, maturity, and interest rate structures. AMD has a $3 billion facility maturing in April 2027 with SOFR-based interest margins between 0.575% and 1.20%, whereas Micron has a smaller $2.5 billion facility maturing earlier in May 2026, with interest described as SOFR plus 1.00% to 1.75% in the adjacent year context. Additionally, AMD explicitly discloses a sustainability-linked pricing component, which is not mentioned in Micron's corresponding disclosure.

sentences.text: As of August 29, 2024, no amounts were outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facility and $2.50 billion was available to us.
Any amounts outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facility would mature in May 2026 and amounts borrowed may be prepaid without penalty.
The Company has $3 billion available under a revolving credit agreement, as amended, that expires on April 29, 2027 (Revolving Credit Agreement).
As of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023, the Company had no outstanding borrowings under the Revolving Credit Agreement.
Each SOFR Loan will bear interest at a rate per annum equal to the applicable SOFR plus a margin between 0.575% and 1.20%.

comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom entered into a five-year, $7.5 billion unsecured revolving credit agreement in January 2021, which includes a $500 million letter of credit facility and allows borrowing and repayment until January 19, 2026. The company had no outstanding borrowings under this facility at the end of both 2024 and 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both Micron and Broadcom report no outstanding borrowings under their revolving credit facilities as of their respective fiscal year-end dates in 2024. The primary difference lies in the facility magnitude and structure: Broadcom’s facility is significantly larger at $7.5 billion (including a $500 million letter of credit sub-facility) maturing in January 2026, while Micron’s is $2.5 billion maturing in May 2026. Broadcom’s disclosure also highlights that outstanding commercial paper reduces available borrowing capacity, a nuance not present in Micron's specific Revolving Credit Facility text.

sentences.text: As of August 29, 2024, no amounts were outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facility and $2.50 billion was available to us.

We had no borrowings outstanding under the revolving credit facility at either November 3, 2024 or October 29, 2023.

comparisons.peer_topic: Revolving Credit Facility Limits and Maturities
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, the company expanded its 5-year $5.0 billion and 364-day $5.0 billion revolving credit facilities to $7.0 billion and $8.0 billion respectively, with maturity dates extended to February 2029 and January 2025. These facilities are unsecured general obligations and had no borrowings outstanding as of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both Micron and Intel disclose zero outstanding borrowings under their revolving credit facilities at the end of fiscal year 2024. They differ substantially in facility size and recent activity: Intel’s facilities are much larger, with a $7.0 billion 5-year facility and an $8.0 billion 364-day facility, both of which were expanded in 2024. In contrast, Micron’s facility is $2.5 billion with no mention of expansion in the current year text. Intel’s facility matures in February 2029 for the 5-year portion, which is significantly later than Micron’s May 2026 maturity.

sentences.text: As of August 29, 2024, no amounts were outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facility and $2.50 billion was available to us.
Any amounts outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facility would mature in May 2026 and amounts borrowed may be prepaid without penalty.

In 2024, we expanded both our 5-year $5.0 billion revolving credit facility agreement and our 364-day $5.0 billion credit facility agreement, to $7.0 billion and $8.0 billion, respectively, and the maturity dates were extended by one year to February 2029 and January 2025, respectively.
The revolving credit facilities had no borrowings outstanding as of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023.
